criteria.criterion: Closing a bug emits no `Ambiguous prefix` diagnostics for commit-subject candidates the user never supplied.
`derive_caused_by` performs work bounded by the number of DISTINCT candidate refs rather than re-resolving per commit, proven by a call-count regression test.
Every id form that resolves today still resolves: full canonical id, 8-hex two-quad prefix, alias, Jira key, and unambiguous bare 4-hex.

The original post-close reproduction, replayed as a regression test over a synthetic multi-commit history, emits no `Ambiguous prefix` text and resolves each DISTINCT ref at most once (no per-commit re-resolution of the bug id).

A regression test asserts that no alias generatable from the wordlist (`adj-noun`, `adj-noun-noun`, or the 8-hex no-dash fallback) can take the 1-, 2-, or 4-quad hex shape rejected by the short-circuit, so the optimization cannot silently drift.

`src/rebar/_ids.py`'s module docstring no longer presents "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as a plain supported form, and `AGENTS.md`'s ticket-identifier paragraph positively names the preferred forms (alias / 8-digit two-quad prefix / full canonical id / Jira ids) while retaining its existing compatibility framing.

Bug 'Enrichment drain treats unrelated short hex fragments as ticket prefixes and hangs post-write commands' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
